# Best AI Voice Agents for Outbound Calling and Lead Qualification in 2026


## Best AI outbound calling platforms at a glance


This is a published-source ranking, not a hands-on test. We ranked the platforms by the available published evidence for multi-step qualification, dialer compatibility, and context-preserving transfers. Where the article does not link to supporting documentation, treat a capability as unverified. Compare deployment requirements and full-stack costs before choosing a platform.


1. **SigmaMind AI:** Best for call centers adding multi-step qualification and context-preserving human handoffs to an existing dialer. SigmaMind AI says it charges no separate concurrency fee. Confirm campaign capacity and total usage costs in a current quote. Buyers seeking a new phone system or a broader AI SDR should compare the other options below.
2. **Retell AI:** Best for developers building qualification workflows with a documented Salesforce integration; confirm dialer and transfer requirements.
3. **CloudTalk:** Best for sales teams considering human dialing and autonomous AI calling in one business phone system.
4. **Bland AI:** Best for enterprises evaluating a bundled voice-pricing quote and security documentation. Confirm the documentation and campaign controls before treating it as suitable for a regulated use case.
5. **Vapi:** Best for developers evaluating a configurable voice stack. Vapi publishes hosting and concurrency prices, but its pricing page alone does not establish the outbound integration or transfer features assessed here.
6. **Synthflow AI:** Best for enterprises scoping a voice-automation deployment. Synthflow AI publishes an annual starting price, but buyers must confirm integrations, concurrency, and handoffs for their deployment.
7. **Thoughtly:** Best for buyers evaluating lead follow-up across voice and SMS.
8. **11x:** Best for buyers seeking a multichannel AI SDR rather than a standalone per-minute calling platform.

## 1. SigmaMind AI: best for qualification on an existing dialer


[SigmaMind AI](https://sigmamind.ai/) is a strong option in this comparison for contact centers, BPOs, and agencies adding voice AI to an existing dialer. SigmaMind AI says it integrates with VICIdial, Five9, NICE, Genesys, and Convoso. Request current documentation and confirm which functions each integration supports in your deployment. Ask SigmaMind AI to demonstrate your specific integration and identify which campaign operations remain in the dialer.


SigmaMind AI describes multi-step workflows that collect answers and apply qualification rules. SigmaMind AI also says its workflows support node-level function calls, workflow records, and warm or cold transfers with conversation context. Request documentation and a demonstration of the context the receiving person actually gets. Ask SigmaMind AI to demonstrate those functions with your qualification rules and connected systems.


SigmaMind AI says it provides voicemail detection, recordings, transcripts, and call outcomes, including termination reasons. Request current documentation for these features. Reviewers can use those records to check whether the agent distinguished voicemail from a live answer and applied qualification rules correctly. Ask SigmaMind AI to demonstrate how its webhooks or APIs send results to your CRM, BI system, or quality-assurance workflow.


SigmaMind AI describes multi-client workspaces with separate tracking and billing. Ask whether the proposed workspace separates access, activity reports, and charges by client.


SigmaMind AI says its pay-as-you-go plan has no subscription or separate concurrency fee and lists a $0.04-per-minute voice platform fee. Confirm those terms against current pricing documentation. Selected STT, TTS, LLM, and telephony services add to the total. Ask SigmaMind AI for a current quote that accounts for those services, campaign capacity, and any charges for SIP trunking or custom telephony. Enterprise pricing requires a custom quote.


## 2. Retell AI: best for developer-led qualification workflows


Retell AI may suit developers building lead-qualification workflows. Confirm its batch-calling capabilities for your campaign. Retell AI documents a[Salesforce integration](https://www.retellai.com/integrations/salesforce) , but buyers should confirm how their qualification results reach it. Ask Retell AI to document transfer behavior and any caller-ID or number-verification features your campaign requires.


A[Retell AI pricing article](https://www.retellai.com/blog/ai-voice-agent-pricing-full-cost-breakdown-platform-comparison-roi-analysis) discusses a rate of about $0.07 per connected minute before other applicable components. Verify that the rate still applies to your configuration. That figure should not be treated as the complete connected-minute price. Ask which speech, language-model, telephony, support, and capacity charges apply to your proposed Retell AI configuration.


Retell AI is worth evaluating when you can build and maintain the required workflows through its APIs rather than relying on an existing call-center dialer to provide them. Nontechnical teams should confirm how much engineering is required for their qualification, CRM, and escalation workflows.


## 3. CloudTalk: best for combined human and AI sales calling


CloudTalk may be worth evaluating if you want human dialing tools and outbound AI agents from one provider. Confirm the current capabilities of each product in CloudTalk's documentation. Ask CloudTalk whether the proposed configuration shares queues and integrations across those tools.


CloudTalk's human dialing specifications should not be used as specifications for its AI calls. Before comparing it with a standalone voice agent, confirm which dialing, voicemail-detection, and live-handoff features apply to AI calls rather than human-operated calls. Ask CloudTalk to document capacity for its human parallel dialer and AI agents separately. Ask CloudTalk which CRM connections support the proposed AI workflow and what information each can read or update.


Request CloudTalk's current phone-system and AI Voice Agents rates, along with applicable telephony and capacity charges, before calculating the full-stack AI cost.


## 4. Bland AI: best for enterprises reviewing security documentation


[Bland AI](https://www.bland.ai/) markets inbound and outbound autonomous phone agents. Ask it to demonstrate lead qualification and warm transfer in your proposed workflow. Ask Bland AI which CRM, contact-center, SIP, and API connections support the outbound workflow you plan to use, and request documentation for each required connection.


Ask Bland AI for current evidence of any security certifications or regulatory assurances relevant to your deployment. Verify the scope and status of each claim. These terms describe different kinds of assurance or compliance requirements, so do not treat the list as a set of equivalent certifications. Review Bland AI's documentation against your security and regulatory requirements. A vendor certification does not make an outbound campaign compliant. Configure consent, disclosures, contact policies, recording, and data handling for your jurisdictions and use case.


Bland AI says its per-minute rate bundles telephony, STT, TTS, and its language model. The reviewed[first-party page](https://www.bland.ai/) does not disclose that rate, so request a quote rather than comparing it with a platform-only fee.[Bland AI says production agents typically deploy in two to six weeks](https://www.bland.ai/) . That vendor estimate is not a guaranteed timeline for a particular integration.


## 5. Vapi: best for teams evaluating a developer-built stack


Vapi's[pricing page](https://vapi.ai/pricing) lists a $0.05-per-minute hosting fee with model costs passed through. The[Vapi pricing page](https://vapi.ai/pricing) lists four included concurrent calls without a package, Core at $29 per month with 10, and Pro at a $999-per-month minimum with 30. It lists additional concurrent lines at $10 per line per month. Confirm current limits and charges before using them in a cost comparison. Hosting and capacity prices do not include every model and transport charge. Vapi’s pricing page alone does not establish its CRM or dialer connections, voicemail detection, transfer behavior, or campaign controls.


For Vapi, request a demonstration of the qualification flow, voicemail outcome, CRM update, and human transfer you need. Add model, voice, transport, and capacity costs to its hosting fee before comparing quotes.


## 6. Synthflow AI: best for enterprise deployments with scoped requirements


[Synthflow AI's pricing page](https://synthflow.ai/pricing) lists enterprise contracts starting at $30,000 annually. The pricing page describes SIP and approved telephony options, CRM and contact-center integrations, routing, escalation paths, and handoffs. Synthflow AI scopes pricing and implementation around factors such as volume, concurrency, telephony, integrations, and launch support.


Synthflow AI's pricing page does not establish a universal per-minute rate or a fixed AI concurrency cap. It also does not establish a rapid launch timeline. Validate the proposed outbound flow, voicemail disposition, live handoff, CRM field mapping, and total contract cost in a scoped demonstration.


## 7. Thoughtly: best for teams evaluating voice and SMS lead follow-up


Thoughtly says its outbound voice and SMS sequences can contact leads, collect qualification answers, and arrange follow-up. The article does not link to documentation for that capability or to its Salesforce loan-officer example. Request both before relying on the example to assess fit. Treat that as a vendor example, not evidence of typical campaign results.


Thoughtly may fit programs that need coordinated voice and text follow-up if its current documentation confirms the sequence your campaign requires. The sources linked in this comparison do not establish Thoughtly's voicemail detection, live warm transfer, concurrency charges, or pricing. Ask Thoughtly for current documentation of the features and controls your campaign requires.


## 8. 11x: best for an autonomous multichannel AI SDR


11x presents Alice as a digital worker for multichannel prospecting rather than a standalone voice API. Request current 11x documentation for its outreach, CRM synchronization, and meeting-booking claims. Confirm the voice-calling functions separately.


Ask 11x for Alice's current annual contract price, prospect allowance, and any charges for onboarding, deliverability support, or mailbox setup. Obtain the current terms in a quote. Ask 11x whether its quote is based on leads, call usage, or both. No linked source here separates 11x's voice costs or verifies voicemail detection, live transfer, or AI calling concurrency pricing.


Evaluate 11x if you want a broader SDR service, but confirm which calling functions and charges its contract includes. If you need direct control over call logic and human transfer, compare those functions in a voice platform demonstration.


## Best AI outbound calling platform by buyer type


### B2B SDR programs


For a B2B SDR program, check whether each platform can qualify a lead, update the CRM, book a meeting, and pass prior answers to a human when needed. SigmaMind AI fits teams that already run campaigns through a contact-center dialer and want multi-step qualification before transferring an interested prospect. Thoughtly is relevant when voice-to-SMS follow-up is central, while 11x suits teams buying a broader autonomous prospecting worker. Retell AI is worth evaluating if you have developers who can assemble and maintain the workflow.


### Insurance


For high-volume insurance prospecting, test whether the agent delivers required disclosures, captures the fields your agency needs, and transfers prospects to an authorized person when required. SigmaMind AI lists multi-step workflows and context-preserving transfers for teams using existing call-center infrastructure. Ask for a demonstration of the required disclosures, captured fields, and transfer to an authorized person. Bland AI is another option if its current security documentation meets the agency’s requirements. Have counsel or your compliance staff review consent, scripts, recording practices, calling windows, and data handling before launch.


### Real estate


For real estate outreach, test property or location qualification, appointment scheduling, CRM updates, and transfer to an available agent. Ask SigmaMind AI to demonstrate that workflow, including what information reaches the agent. Thoughtly is worth considering when prospects frequently move between calls and text messages. Test interruptions, incomplete answers, and callback requests rather than evaluating only ideal scripts.


### Debt collection


Debt collection requires tightly controlled identity verification, disclosures, contact policies, escalation rules, and recordkeeping. Ask Retell AI to demonstrate the identity checks, disclosures, contact restrictions, and escalation rules your collection campaign requires. SigmaMind AI says it provides workflow records, recordings, transcripts, termination reasons, and call-center integrations. Request documentation and verify that each capability supports the collection process you intend to run. Product features do not replace legal review. Collection agencies must configure each campaign for applicable federal, state, and local requirements.


### Agencies managing multiple clients


Agencies running campaigns for multiple clients need separate access, analytics, credentials, and billing for each client. SigmaMind AI describes multi-client workspaces with separate tracking and billing, plus integrations with VICIdial, Five9, NICE, Genesys, and Convoso. Verify client access controls and the required integration functions in a demonstration. SigmaMind AI does not list a separate concurrency fee, although you should confirm available campaign capacity if several clients may call at once. Agencies considering other vendors should verify tenant isolation and client-level billing rather than assuming a standard workspace supports both.


## How this published-source comparison was ranked


The ranking weighs documented qualification steps, connected-system updates, voicemail handling, and context-preserving transfers. Capabilities without supporting documentation remain unverified.


For example, an insurance agency could ask whether a prospect wants a quote, capture the requested coverage and preferred callback time, then use those answers to update the CRM. It could transfer an interested prospect to an authorized person with the prior answers or record a callback disposition. If the call reaches voicemail or goes unanswered, record that outcome instead of marking the lead qualified. Use this workflow to test each vendor; the comparison does not establish that every platform supports every step.


We did not conduct hands-on tests of all eight vendors. This ranking compares SigmaMind AI's published workflow, telephony, analytics, and pricing descriptions with available first-party information from competitors. A listed integration or feature does not establish how it will work in your deployment, so capabilities without supporting documentation are marked unverified.


The ranking considered:


1. **Outbound workflow depth:** multi-step qualification, exception handling, and human escalation.
2. **Dialer and CRM compatibility:** whether the platform can work with established campaign infrastructure and business records.
3. **Transfer and voicemail handling:** whether these functions were explicitly documented rather than inferred.
4. **Cost transparency:** separation of platform, telephony, STT, TTS, LLM, subscription, and concurrency costs.
5. **Operational control:** analytics, recordings, transcripts, auditability, and multi-client administration.
6. **Compliance controls:** documented security or campaign controls, without treating vendor certifications as proof that a specific campaign is lawful.


Custom pricing is identified separately from published rates. Vendor case studies and performance claims were not treated as independent benchmarks.


## How to choose an AI outbound calling platform


Start with your telephony architecture. If you want to keep your dialer, check whether a voice platform can use its existing pacing, routing, reporting, and agent workflows. If you plan to replace it, compare those functions in the proposed phone system as well. If you use VICIdial, Five9, NICE, Genesys, or Convoso, ask SigmaMind AI to demonstrate how its integration preserves the campaign operations you need.


Test a qualification flow using real campaign conditions, including interruptions, corrected answers, voicemail, and unavailable human agents. Compare captured fields and qualification decisions with recordings and transcripts. Check CRM dispositions and ask the receiving person whether they got the prior answers. Track errors and outcomes for your own calls rather than treating vendor case studies as comparable accuracy scores.


Calculate the full-stack cost after confirming the proposed call flow and integrations. Ask each vendor to itemize the following costs.


- Platform or subscription fees
- Telephony and phone-number charges
- Speech-to-text usage
- Text-to-speech and premium-voice usage
- LLM usage
- Concurrency or capacity charges
- Implementation, support, and compliance add-ons


Use the same expected call duration, connection rate, and usage assumptions for each quote. Check which services each quote includes so you do not mistake a platform-only rate for the total cost.


Before launch, have counsel or your compliance team review the use case and jurisdictions. Include consent records, Do Not Call suppression, calling windows, disclosures, and recording practices in that review. The[FCC states that TCPA restrictions on artificial or prerecorded voices apply to AI-generated human voices](https://www.fcc.gov/document/fcc-confirms-tcpa-applies-ai-technologies-generate-human-voices/gomez-statement) . A vendor's security controls or dialing features do not establish that a particular campaign is lawful.


## FAQs


**What is AI outbound calling?**


AI outbound calling uses a voice agent to place calls, conduct conversations, record outcomes, and complete actions such as qualification, scheduling, CRM updates, or human transfer. An autonomous voice agent conducts the conversation, while an AI-assisted dialer supports a human caller. Available actions vary by product and configuration.


**What is an AI dialer?**


An AI dialer automates or assists with placing calls. Some products also use a voice agent to converse with the person who answers. Some AI voice products place calls through their own dialing tools, while others connect to an existing dialer or phone system. SigmaMind AI is an example of the latter approach. Confirm whether a proposed product actually performs the dialing or relies on a connected system.


**Can AI make cold calls?**


Yes, the technology can place outbound prospecting calls. Whether a campaign is permitted requires a review of consent, recipient and number type, message, jurisdiction, and applicable calling rules. A vendor’s compliance features do not replace legal advice or campaign-level controls.


**How does automated lead qualification work?**


The voice agent asks required questions, captures answers, applies defined rules, and records the result. Depending on its configuration, the agent may schedule a meeting, write the qualification result to the CRM, or transfer an interested prospect to a human. Multi-step workflows are useful when qualification depends on several answers or external system checks.


**How much does AI outbound calling cost?**


Costs may include a subscription or platform rate, telephony, phone numbers, STT, TTS, LLM usage, concurrency, implementation, and support. SigmaMind AI lists a $0.04-per-minute voice platform fee and says it charges no separate concurrency fee. Request a quote for the remaining usage components.


**Is AI outbound calling compliant?**


No platform makes every campaign automatically compliant. Buyers must configure consent, suppression lists, calling policies, disclosures, recording, data retention, and human oversight for the laws and contractual requirements that apply to them.


**Can an AI calling platform integrate with a CRM?**


Yes, when the vendor provides a native integration, API, webhook, or automation connector. Verify whether the integration can read lead context, write dispositions and qualification fields, create follow-up tasks, and preserve the transcript or summary.


**Can AI detect voicemail?**


Some platforms can. SigmaMind AI says it offers voicemail detection, while CloudTalk describes automatic voicemail detection for its human dialing tools. Request current documentation and verify whether detection applies to the AI calls you plan to make. The feature was not publicly verified for every platform in this comparison.


**What is a warm transfer?**


A warm transfer passes the call to a human with relevant context and may keep the AI on the line until the person answers. SigmaMind AI describes context-preserving warm and cold transfers. Ask CloudTalk whether its AI calling product supports a live handoff and when it passes the call context to a person. Confirm the behavior in the configuration you plan to use.
